priorArt.source: Ethereum gas and fees: technical overview
priorArt.influence: Use enforced workload limits and metered/reserved capacity rather than repeatedly predicting complete future execution scenarios. This is a design analogy, not adoption of Ethereum's gas ledger, fees or consensus.
priorArt.limit: Ethereum can revert state changes on execution exhaustion. Previously signed, published or admitted room work creates obligations that cannot simply be undone; its complete finishing capacity must remain available. No Ethereum throughput-to-FPS equivalence or performance guarantee is inferred.

priorArt.source: Balegas et al., Extending Eventually Consistent Cloud Databases for Enforcing Numeric Invariants (2015)
priorArt.influence: Escrow/bounded-counter reasoning: establish exclusive finite capacity before accepting obligations, and preserve the invariant as work changes. This informs the finishing-reserve/incremental-admission direction through existing owners.
priorArt.limit: No new replicated rights system or second accounting ledger is adopted. The paper does not prove this protocol's authentication, native storage, recovery, charge accounting or drainability.

priorArt.source: Fryer et al., Recon: Verifying File System Consistency at Runtime (FAST 2012), sections 2.2-2.4
priorArt.influence: Closest structural analogy: start from a complete validated state, then check change-local inductive obligations rather than rescan the whole system. This informed the proposed source-bound incremental application-resource projection.
priorArt.limit: Completeness of the initial state, faithful change observation and lower-layer assumptions are essential. Reusable numerical/parsing facts are not fresh admission authority; native currency and corruption checks remain independently required.

priorArt.source: Bailis et al., Coordination Avoidance in Database Systems (Extended Version)
priorArt.influence: Coordination avoidance must be justified against exact operations and invariants, not assumed from eventual convergence or a signed DAG.
priorArt.limit: Arbitrary application reducers are not assumed commutative or append-only. Grid's max-per-ID resource upper bound may be incrementally accumulated without changing the order-sensitive actual reducer or accepted state.
